subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should every public/operator `cron run` outcome record only observational last-run data while never changing scheduler counters, backoff, next-run timing, enabled state, failure alerts, or one-shot consumption?
rationale: The linked bug clearly requires preventing destructive manual consumption, but extending that rule to all scheduler-owned state and persisting manual attribution defines the permanent operator-run contract and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Approve fully non-consuming operator runs
options.body: Keep the internal origin design and treat timer and watcher-terminal as the only owners of scheduler state and one-shot consumption.

options.title: Narrow to deletion protection
options.body: Prevent manual one-shot deletion but retain selected existing counter, alert, or timing mutations for operator runs.

options.title: Add an explicit consuming mode
options.body: Preserve safe operator defaults while designing a separate maintainer-approved API or CLI action for intentionally consuming scheduler semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve fully non-consuming operator runs
recommendation.body: Keep the internal origin design and treat timer and watcher-terminal as the only owners of scheduler state and one-shot consumption.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history and timeline make this the best available routing candidate for the cross-cutting cron service contract decision.
